title: Take the constant out of the gap

blocks.text: A water utility's pump-replacement model reports its objective as "total network value": the value of the replacements it chooses **plus** a fixed amount $`K`$ for the network that already exists. The solver's relative gap divides by that total, so its reports look better than the decisions deserve. The analytics team wants every report to carry the gap on the part the decisions control.
Write `true_gap(incumbent, bound, constant)` in `true_gap.py`. `incumbent` and `bound` are the two numbers the solver reported, both including `constant`. Return a dict:

items: `"absolute"`: $`|\text{bound} - \text{incumbent}|`$. The constant cancels out of this difference.
`"seen"`: the absolute gap divided by $`|\text{incumbent}|`$, which is what the solver saw.
`"on_decisions"`: the absolute gap divided by $`|\text{incumbent} - \text{constant}|`$, the value of the decisions alone.

blocks.text: The model may be a maximization or a minimization, and the constant may be negative (a sunk cost taken off every plan). Both ratios are `0.0` when the absolute gap is 0, and `math.inf` when their denominator is 0 and the absolute gap is not.

cases.says: with a large constant the gap on the decisions is far larger than the gap the solver saw
with no constant the gap seen and the gap on the decisions are the same
on a minimization, with the bound below the incumbent, every gap is still positive
a negative constant, such as a sunk cost, is removed by subtracting it, which raises the decisions' part
when the incumbent is all constant and the gap is not zero, the gap on the decisions is infinite

origin.section: A Constant in the Objective Shrinks the Relative Gap Without Improving the Plan

concepts: a constant in the objective adds to the solver's denominator, so the gap on the decisions is the absolute gap over the objective without it
